modeling_notes: Reveal process allows adversary to trigger key compromise at any time via in(any) then out(sk), with preceding Reveal(pk) event.
Secrecy lemmas use weak disjunction: either the adversary never knows na, or the relevant public key (pkB) is revealed at some time.
Secret events now include the encryption public key (pkB) to link the secret to the key needed for compromise in lemmas.
Executability lemma relies on Send/Recv events that carry the same message term m over the network.
expected_limitations: secrecy_PFS_A is expected to falsify (CounterexampleFound) because after-the-fact Reveal of pkB allows decryption of the recorded ciphertext.
secret_A and secret_B are weak secrecy properties that trivially hold if a Reveal event occurs; they may need strengthening for stronger guarantees.
